text:
anna: Quick heads-up — after merging the AWQ packing change (PR #3421) I'm seeing a regression on 7B INT8 serving. p50 tokens up ~10% at seq_len 2048 on our nightly perf rig. attaching numbers and a tiny profile snapshot.

anna: bench snapshot:
```
model: redwood/gpt-7b-awq
seq_len: 2048
baseline (pre-PR): p50 token latency = 59ms
post-PR: p50 token latency = 65ms
pack_cpu_time: 12.1ms (was 3.8ms)
gpu_kernel_time: 46.0ms (was 48.5ms)
end-to-end: 68.4ms (was 59.2ms)
```

mike: rough q: did kernel selector start falling back more often? any calib/threshold tweaks in the deploy?

sophia: we did change the packing order to do layer-contiguous pack (to reduce peak memory) and shifted packing to the main CPU thread for simplicity. that saved memory spikes but added extra memcpy/serialize work on the hot path.

anna: that's my suspicion too. profile flame shows long periods of `pack_block` on CPU blocking worker threads. also noticed KV cache hit-rate drops slightly because the reorder changes layout for prepacked keys.

drew: can you paste the microbench command you ran? i'll run a few variants.

anna: ran this:
```bash
./run_bench --model redwood/gpt-7b-awq --seq 2048 --group-size 128 --pack-workers 1 --kv-cache on --warmup 200 --iters 200
```

perf-bot: auto-report: kernel_selector: INT8_GEMM chosen=7400, fallback_fp16=420, pack_calls=1800, pack_time_total_ms=21600

mike: fallback_fp16=420 seems high. our kernel chooser has a calibration variance check (vdrop < 0.02) that gates using the INT8 fast GEMM. did the new packing change the calibration buffer ordering?

sophia: yes — the pack ordering changed the per-group layout we feed to the calib aggregator. aggregator uses contiguous group means to compute scale var. reorder can skew variance if groups near boundary get mixed sizes.

drew: suggestion — run bisect on group-size and pack-workers to measure tradeoffs. my hunch: larger group_size reduces kernel count (fewer small GEMMs) but increases pack CPU cost and memory working set. try 64/128/256.

anna: I ran a quick sweep:
```
group 64: p50 67ms, pack_time 9ms, fallback_fp16 510
group 128: p50 65ms, pack_time 12ms, fallback_fp16 420
group 256: p50 70ms, pack_time 20ms, fallback_fp16 300
```
So group=128 looks best of the three overall, but pack_time is still the hotspot. fallback counts drop with larger groups, which helps GPU, but pack CPU increases.

mike: okay. that matches a packing vs kernel tradeoff. two orthogonal fixes: 1) move packing off the main thread to dedicated pack worker pool (parallel memcpy), 2) make kernel selector invariant to group ordering by aggregating calib stats per-weight instead of per-packed-block. both sound like low-risk changes.

sophia: moving packing to workers will add context-switch and queue latency — we should bench pack-workers=2/4. also consider prepack caching keyed by (model, group_size, layout_hash) so KV cache reuse improves.

anna: quick test with pack-workers=4 and group=128:
```
./run_bench --model redwood/gpt-7b-awq --seq 2048 --group-size 128 --pack-workers 4 --kv-cache on
result: p50 61ms, pack_time 4.5ms, fallback_fp16 418
```
That's promising: pack_time dropped and p50 almost back to baseline, but fallback_fp16 roughly same — so kernel selector issue still present.

drew: can you dump the kernel selection logs for a single request? look for why those ~400 fallbacks happen. maybe a numerical instability in calibration when pack ordering changes.

anna: pasted snippet from runtime log: 
```
[1776543233] kernel_selector: layer=7 group=3 calib_mean=0.0038 calib_var=0.021 -> veto INT8, fallback fp16
[1776543233] kernel_selector: layer=7 group=4 calib_mean=0.0035 calib_var=0.019 -> choose INT8
```
so some groups are just over the variance threshold. the reorder shuffles values and some groups straddle the threshold.

mike: threshold too brittle. two options: widen threshold slightly (e.g., 0.025) or use a smoothed per-weight variance (EWMA) so transient reorder doesn't flip decisions. both affect accuracy guarantees — need evals.

sophia: let's avoid a heuristic that magically increases error. prefer moving packing off the critical path + change aggregator to per-weight EWMA over recent requests (not just current request) so decisions are workload-stable.

perf-bot: eval-run queued: eval-job #998 for perplexity/regression on validation-set (calib-threshold chgs)

anna: action items from thread:
- bisect group-size and pack-workers (anna/drew) — try 64/128/256 & 1/2/4 workers.
- implement pack worker pool + async memcpy (sophia) — small patch to move pack_block to pack threadpool.
- make kernel selector aggregate per-weight EWMA stats and expose debug counters (mike) — we need to lower fallback spikes without changing final model quality.
- add prepack KV cache keying by layout_hash to improve reuse (sophia/anna).

mike: I'll add instrumentation: metric: kernel_fallback_rate per-layer, pack_cpu_ms, pack_queue_time_ms. set alert if fallback_rate increases >3x vs baseline.

anna: great. i'll start the bisect on the perf rig and drop results here. thanks y'all :thumbsup:

sophia: thanks — i'll prototype pack-worker change in a branch and post perf numbers once ready.

drew: tagging @sre for nightly-rig scheduling if we need more runs.

perf-bot: scheduled 3 additional runs on rig-3 between 03:30-04:30 UTC.
